claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 18 years old and lives with me at home. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have one child, Alex, who is 18 years old and lives with you.

Since Alex is over 16, his eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether he's in approved education or training. Child Benefit can continue for children under 20 if they stay in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as A-levels, further education college, or an approved training course)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school but hasn't gone on to study anything further.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I need to ask a few more questions to fully assess Alex's situation.

**Is Alex currently working? If so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I have a couple more questions to determine Alex's eligibility.

**Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services? If he left education or training recently (within the last 20 weeks), this could affect his eligibility.**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't signed up with any careers service or the armed forces.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have one final question:

**Is Alex currently claiming any benefits in his own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit based on what you've told me.

I now have enough information to make a determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**I'm sorry, but you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why: Since Alex is 18 years old (over 16), Child Benefit can only continue if he stays in approved education or training. As Alex has finished school and is not currently in any further education, training, or apprenticeship, he does not meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

**However, please note:** If Alex decides to return to approved education or training in the future, or if he registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services within 20 weeks of leaving education, you may be able to claim Child Benefit again. If his circumstances change, you can contact HMRC to discuss your eligibility at that time.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
